Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Q2 & H1 FY27 Earnings Call of Jana 
Small Finance Bank hosted by Systematix Group. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in 
the listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the 
presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during this conference call, please signal an 
operator by pressing star then zero on your touch-tone phone. 
 
I now hand the conference call over to Mr. Gaurav Purohit from Systematix Group. Thank you, 
and over to you, sir. 
Gaurav Purohit: 
Thank you, Iqra. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to Jana Small Finance Bank's Q2 & 
H1 FY27 Earnings Call. On behalf of Systematix Group, I would like to thank the Jana 
management team for giving us the opportunity to host this call. We are pleased to have with us 
today the bank's senior management team led by Mr. Ajay Kanwal, Managing Director and 
CEO; Mr. K. S. Raman, Executive Director; Mr. Abhilash Sandur, Chief Financial Officer; 
along with other members of the senior management team. 
 
With that, I would like to hand over the call to Ajay sir for his opening remarks, following which 
we will open the floor for questions. Over to you, sir. 
Ajay Kanwal: 
Thank you so much, and good evening to everyone. As always, we will refer to the investor 
deck, which you have loaded on, and we will talk through a few specific slides, and then we 
would welcome Q&A, rather questions from all of you. 
 
Let's move to Slide number 3. In Slide number 3, there are a very important few points to note. 
Q2 has been the highest ever PBT we had in our history. Having seen our Q2 performance, 
which now if you add the Q1, it reaches INR326 crores, which is equal to the PAT of last year 
of INR326 crores. Hence, we would like to take our guidance up, which was originally increase 
of 80% in PAT to 100% of PAT. So we should double our PAT this year versus last year. 
 
A few of the key drivers which are getting us there. First is our net interest margins at 7.54% for 
Q2 up from 6.5% last Q2. And one of the contributors to this net interest margin improvement, 
other than the various components which have gone into build the asset book, we've obviously 
seen a growth of MFI, which was a negative growth till last year. That has helped improve the 
NIMs. And of course, cost of funds is down from 7.9% to 7.4%. So a good combination of 
slightly better mix on the loan side and drop in cost of funds. 
 
I'm very glad to report that our best ever PBT is accompanied by growth in secured assets, which 
has seen a secular improvement year-on-year, and now we stand at 73.7%. For folks who are 
joining this call the first time, we have several times said that our intention is to be around 80% 
of secured assets, and that we consider as a good answer. 
 
I must say, while secured assets, improvement in NIMs, our operating costs has seen a 15% 
year-on-year increase. On the right side, you can see a graph which explains that how the jaws 
is widening, which is cost run rate is much lower than the revenue run rate. And that has become 
very healthy this quarter because the net interest income is up 35%, cost up 15%.

So, you've got a positive jaws of 20%. But very importantly, absolute cost in Q2 is lower than 
Q1, marginally so, but yet we have been able to arrest cost. I can also tell you with great certainty 
that the likelihood of cost remaining muted and us getting more operating leverage for our 
business is a fairly highly likely expectation that you should have. So cost under control, NIMs 
are getting better, secured assets are growing. 
 
Finally, we should talk about how the quality of the book is, which is in terms of portfolio health. 
Gross NPA is down to 2.17%. Our net NPA is up at 1.08%. We normally do extra provision to 
drop net NPA below 1%. But this time, we have chosen to wait because we have lodged our 
claims for the guarantee program, which is about INR68 crores. That will comfortably get us 
below 1% moment the claims are realized. 
 
So rather than provision now and then work around the whole accounting system next quarter 
again once this claim comes, we have chosen that we will go to 1.08%. And then once the claim 
is received, which we already lodged, I think we will anyway come below 1%. So all-in-all, a 
very, very healthy quarter. But importantly, when it comes to cost, when it comes to NPA, when 
it comes to NIMs, it is signalling that we're going to have a very good year. 
 
I will now move to the next page, Page number 4. I've already mentioned the gross NPA and 
how that has moderated. I want to draw your attention on this page to the chart below, which is 
on the SMA and slippages. So in quarter 1, we had a marginal increase in SMA growth. It led to 
a slight increase in slippages, and we had two one-offs one is a secured loan, which has gone 
into NPA where we have collateral, which covers it and a small impact in the MFI book of 
drought, both in Assam, Maharashtra and Karnataka, which impacted 0.3% of slippages. 
 
Given that Q2 SMA has dropped over Q1, you should naturally expect that slippages will be 
lower in Q3. Secondly, with these one-offs not being there, it will certainly be lower than Q2. 
So that's something that I did want to give you a heads up on how the book is looking and what 
we expect. And what it translates in terms of credit cost, I would probably ask you to wait for 
Page number 6, but let me first cover Page 5, and this is an important page. 
 
Yes. Good evening again, folks. So I'm on Page number 5, very important page. You can see 
our total unsecured book gross NPA is INR673 crores. The provisions we have against is 
INR377 crores, leaving uncovered book of INR296 crores. But this INR296 crores is completely 
under the guarantee program. In fact, the guarantee program is at INR319 crores, of which I had 
mentioned earlier that we have already lodged INR68 crores as claims and the balance INR251 
crores, we would lodge next year in Q3 again. 
 
So from a variety of perspectives, I think one is, obviously, the collection efficiencies have gone 
up and has been at 99%, which we will talk of when we go to the asset page. More importantly, 
the old slippages for which we have been paying guarantee commission over the last, I would 
say, we began in November '24, so it's nearly 18 to 20 months, we have been paying this 
commission. We are finally seeing some result of that. And that we will see this year and the 
following year. So I think that's an important one.

The other piece I want the investors to note is we had said that all the new disbursements, we 
will continue putting under the guarantee program. The CGFMU program is right now not open 
for fresh guarantees to be added to it. The scheme is going through an approval process. But 
what we have done is we expect that to get reopened soon. 
 
We have assumed that will be open. We have taken the 1% that is required to put it in the 
program, and we've already accrued for it. So, our results today that you see of INR170 crores 
of profit already has an accrual, which is waiting to be used once the CGFMU program opens 
up. 
 
Our guidance of 100% growth in PAT also assumes that we will get our entire portfolio even in 
the next half under the CGFMU and CGTMSE programs. Having said that, I did want to give 
you the factual picture, which is right now, the CGFMU portal is not open for the fresh ones. 
And once it opens, we will do the entire thing. But P&L-wise, we already accounted for it, and 
there will be no change or impact other than what you have already seen in our numbers in terms 
of PAT and our guidance for the second half. 
 
I should move to Page number 6. Here, you can see the clear expectation from our end is we'll 
be under 2% this financial year in terms of credit cost. If you add up the first half, it is 0.43% 
and 0.49%. That comes out to a 0.92% for the first half. We do expect second half, which is 
quarter 3 starting, slippages to get lower. So I would expect that our second half credit cost will 
be lower than the first half. Overall, certainly below 2%. I think that was the most important 
point here. 
 
I will now move on to Page number 8, and this does discuss a few things about our advances. 
So first is our growth, which is 22% year-on-year at INR38,752 crores. Secured obviously 
growing faster at 24%. Our disbursements in the second quarter, which is INR4,414 crores is 
7% higher year-on-year and 5% quarter-on-quarter. We don't normally add up the NBFC 
disbursements because they're lumpy and any quarter can look a little bit odd because of it, and 
we have been doing that for some time. 
 
I want to talk a bit about the MFI book because I think that's been a key part of how things have 
turned around so dramatically for us. Other than the 99% collections, you can see that on the 
next page, MFI book is not growing too fast. And in an MFI market where we can see that the 
number of players are lower, there is less capital and liquidity for many players who are very 
active, normally would expect an MFI book growth to be very strong. 
 
But given that there have been enough and more customers who have not so good histories in 
the credit bureau, the MFI growth is a bit more subdued. The good news is also that our criteria 
is slightly tighter, and I have given a simple variable here. 97% of all my customers have less 
than or equal to two MFIs versus 93% for the industry. 
 
Our collection efficiency already met. And this time, I must add that our 99% collection 
efficiency is not just on the Jana collections, but all our BCs. And our BC book has been one of 
the problems in the past, but I'm glad to report that they are also in the 99% bucket with us.

Our gold loan had a slow quarter. Our Q1 was very strong, Q2 was flattish. The primary reason 
here is that our big growth came in January '26 to March '26. And a big chunk of about 65% to 
70% of these loans were 6-month loans. So they all came up for renewals and interest servicing 
in Q2 this year. And with the drop in gold price, many of the folks had to pay their margins and 
serve their interest components, etcetera. 
 
So it's been a slow quarter growth because the entire chain has been working hard on making 
sure that there is a very smooth transition given the change in gold prices, etcetera. We really 
have seen customers respond very responsibly. But of course, there is timing and work, which 
is why I think a lot of the salespeople have been busy getting this addressed. We should resume 
good growth starting Q3 again. 
 
I did want to talk about vehicle loans because our vehicle loans, which were primarily 2-wheelers 
in the past, now include 2-wheelers and used cars. 2-wheelers are now offered in 135 cities and 
used cars in 50 cities. I did want to mention it because the vehicle loans have a 76% year-on-
year growth. It will maintain very robust growth, not for any change in credit criteria or any 
aggression on our side. 
 
We just are available in so many geographies. If we just expand geographies, the growth will 
sustain. How many geographies are we present in for our affordable housing micro LAP? We're 
in about 220-odd cities. That's the number of cities that 2-wheelers and used cars can get up to. 
We normally give you a bar graph explaining which state concentration there is. And we think 
that it has been so consistent for so long that we don't give you half a page of that information. 
So we've just added a line here, which says the top seven state concentration is at 67% with the 
top three at 37%. 
 
So that's a bit of preamble on our asset business. I would now like you to turn to Page number 
9. And here is where our biggest asset book today in secured assets i.e. affordable housing. It is 
growing at 28.2% year-on-year with an average ticket size of INR11.9 lakhs. Micro LAP, we 
have slowed down. We intend to pick it up, but slowly and surely is our effort. That is on micro 
LAP. 
 
MSME, I'd signalled earlier, is going to be one of our fastest growth engines. It has a 20.6% 
growth year-on-year. I would expect it to grow strongly and robustly. NBFC is 0.7%. Given that 
we'll have enough and more assets growing at our end, we are not really expecting to grow the 
NBFC term loans in any significant way. 
 
Vehicle loans, we already spoke of 76%. Gold loans year-on-year, 81%, though, of course, 
quarter has been tepid at 0.3%. Others typically is employee loans and FD/ODs, nothing 
consequential from a P&L perspective, but we did have one large FD/OD closure, which is why 
it is showing a quarter-on-quarter slight drop. 
 
Unsecured advances year-on-year is 17% growth, but the quarterly growth is at negative 0.3%, 
like I said, that given that we are tight on the credit criteria and there is a huge population, which 
is possibly unable to borrow, we are not seeing aggressive growth here, which is absolutely fine 
by us because we do want to have only good growth. So we'll keep trying to grow, but not

bank is focused on doing multiple relationship with customers. This page specifically for our 
investors who are seeing it first time is on the housing loan and micro LAP book, where our

And you can see a good disbursal of where all these relationships lie, primarily from preapproved

more room there. Our 2-wheeler penetration is still low at 1.1%. And of course, our TD

we expect customers to use Jana as a preferred bank. And this is where we do expect operating 
leverage to really play a role with us.

13%, TD is 17.5%. We have work to do on CASA, and we are committing that you will see a 
very different CASA growth in the second half. We have been a bit more focused on the TD in 
the first half. Our total liability book is now at INR38,221 crores. 
 
Irrespective of the TD and CASA growth rate, our cost of funds remained stable at 7.4% both in 
Q1 and Q2 and is down from Q2 last year of 7.9% and it's got a very healthy mix of noncallable, 
bulk and retail. And we've always maintained this that our contractual bookings is never short 
term, so 96.1% of deposits are 1 year and above. 
 
So I just want to tell everyone that, yes, we have very strong plans to grow CASA. It hasn't 
picked up to our expectation in the first half, but we are very comfortable both on liquidity and 
though the interest rates don't look very simplistic, interest rates are slightly harder in Q2 than 
Q1. But we do want to do our best to make sure that cost of funds remain where they are at this 
point of time. 
 
I will now move on to the financial slide, and I'll ask Abhilash to take you through some key 
financial slides so that you get a good flavour on some of our ratios. 
Abhilash Sandur: 
So, I'm now in Slide number 16, which is explaining the numbers for half year period. Like Ajay 
mentioned earlier, the quarter has been the highest ever PBT quarter for us. Half year profit is 
equal to last year full year profits of INR326 crores. Our ROA has improved to 1.4%. Our ROE 
is currently close to 14%. Book value per share is at INR455 per share. 
 
And our opex, while quarter-on-quarter has been flat, if I look at H1 against H1, that's around 
15% - 16% growth in opex. That's how we have been managed to have a PPOP growth of almost 
27% year-on-year. And then we have continued to be comfortable in capital adequacy with 20% 
CRAR. NNPA, like Ajay mentioned, 1.08%. With the claim coming in, it will be below 1%. 
And share of secured assets is at 73.7%. These are the key numbers, which I wanted to cover in 
Slide number 16.

where we have also disclosed the NIM and yield on advances. We are able to hold on to the 
NIMs of previous quarter. And our NIMs have improved by 1% year-on-year, 6.5% for H1 
FY26. Currently, we are at 7.5%. The cost-to-income ratio, if you see from Q1, which was 
67.0%, has reduced to 64.3% for Q2. These are the three important points which I wanted to

the ROA has improved. The revenues are on upward trend. The jaws is widening in terms of 
opex versus income. So that's the other key element which I wanted to highlight in terms of 
financials. 
 
The cost-to-income ratio currently is at 64%. We are moving towards a 60% benchmark, which 
we set out towards, and that probably will be over the few quarters coming up, while the jaws 
widen in terms of opex and income. Having said that, our total revenue currently has grown by 
18% year-on-year, and quarter-on-quarter, it's at 4% growth. 
 
So, I wanted to also bring up certain elements of P&L, which we have called out in Slide number 
20, which included processing fee, insurance income and liability fee, where we have given the 
details of other income as well. So these are the key metrics which I wanted to cover as part of 
P&L.  
So, guidance, like we mentioned in the initial slide, Guidance has been revised from 80% in 
PAT growth to 100% in PAT growth after considering the profits of H1 being equivalent to the 
profits of full year last year. So we have revised the guidance, and we are confident that this is 
achievable by the looks of it by what we have seen in the trends in the Q1 and Q2. While we are 
maintaining the guidance for both advances and deposits at 19% to 21% for advances and 23% 
to 25% for deposits.

Okay. We will open the floor for questions now. Thank you so much.

is from the line of Jai Chauhan from Yes Securities. 
Jai Chauhan: 
So I just wanted to ask slippages for the period has increased during the period. I guess from 
here, do we expect slippages to show a downward or upward trend over the coming quarters? 
Ajay Kanwal: 
Yes. So I think a few things, Jai, I must tell you, which is, first, the primary challenge always in 
a book of a small finance bank who has microfinance is always MFI. But MFI is, touchwood, 
going through 99% collection rates. Small addition we had in Q2 versus Q1 was primarily in

one-offs in Q2. One was a midsized loan where we will have some time to make sure the 
collateral is fully sold and we recover our money. But meanwhile, it has come into our slippage, 
which has added 0.2%. The drought has given us 0.3%. Both these are one-offs. They should 
drop off in the next quarter. And then you can also see the SMA has also graduated down in Q2,

Or was the decline primarily driven by a time-related sector?

you one of the headcount reasons. So obviously, the MFI stress came down. So we obviously 
had to put a lot of collectors into the MFI business. As you can see, the amount we are collecting

collections.

so obviously, we see some costs coming down. Some of the AI-led processes, which are 
collections calling on both secured and unsecured, welcome calling for new customers, etcetera. 
Those have kicked in, and that has caused us to have some amount of reduction in headcount. 
We've also consciously focused more on our direct sourcing percentage improving over DSA
